analysis.title: US Macro Snapshot: October CPI Preview
key_insights: Natixis expects October inflation to ease from September's pace and mark the start of a trend of subdued prints. Core CPI is forecast at +0.22% m/m and headline CPI at +0.29% m/m, both in line with consensus.

No y/y CPI print will be published for October because of last year's government shutdown. If the print matches Natixis's forecast, the 3m annualized rate stays at 3.4% and the 6m annualized rate falls to 2.5%.

Natixis attributes the expected core slowdown to a reversion in shelter prices, mainly owners' equivalent rent and lodging away from home. Stable diesel prices should also ease price pressure in energy-intensive goods.
A print in line with the forecast would be encouraging to the Fed but still too high to rule out another hike. Natixis expects a hike in December, followed by an extended pause.

Natixis sees little inflationary impulse from the labor market despite its stability, and expects supply-side price pressures to fade. Financial conditions have moved closer to neutral, so the Fed should hesitate to overtighten if disinflation continues in line with the forecast.
Natixis says September's CPI was higher than expected, but it still sees little evidence of a reacceleration. It expects price growth to drift lower in coming quarters, along an uneven path.

tension_points.bull_case: Sticky inflation above target and a stable, perhaps strengthening, labor market warrant another hike in December, even if October CPI matches Natixis's forecast.
tension_points.bear_case: Supply-side price pressures should fade and financial conditions are closer to neutral. With growth headwinds and fragile markets, the Fed should hesitate to overtighten after December if disinflation continues.
tension_points.what_invalidates: October CPI printing in line with the forecast would still be too high to rule out a hike. A strong October Employment Situation Report would reinforce the December hike call.

theme_stances.key_argument: Shelter reversion and stable diesel prices should slow core CPI and begin a trend of subdued prints.
Inflation is sticky and the labor market is stable, so a December hike is warranted before an extended pause.
